Test Objective: Verify atomic one-time OTP consumption when two password-reset requests race concurrently.
Preconditions: A registered account has one valid, unexpired, unused six-digit OTP. Two different new passwords are available and each independently satisfies the documented password rules. The test runner can dispatch both requests concurrently and can verify which password became active.

Test Objective: Verify that SQL syntax in a rule-conforming new password is treated as data and does not damage another account's reset path.
Preconditions: Accounts A and B are registered. Each has its own valid, unexpired, unused six-digit OTP. The password Aa1!';DROP TABLE users;-- satisfies the documented minimum rules through its uppercase, lowercase, digit, allowed exclamation mark, and length.
Request Input: Step 1: Send POST /api/reset-password with Content-Type: application/json and body {"email":"<account-A-email>","resetToken":"<account-A-valid-OTP>","newPassword":"Aa1!';DROP TABLE users;--"}. Expected Result: Account A's reset succeeds and the supplied password is treated only as data. Account B's reset also succeeds, demonstrating that the injected password did not damage the users data path.

Assumptions / Notes: Human-authored case. The second account provides an observable integrity check; proving parameterized storage may still require implementation or database inspection.
